summary: Stephen H. Phillips works in philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the University of Texas at Austin as professor of philosophy (attested 1999) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Stephen Harris is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of New Mexico by 2014 and became University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Stephen J. Laumakis specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West. In 2013, he was attested as Professor of Philosophy and Honors Program Director at the University of St. Thomas.

Stephen Jenkins studied Buddhist and religious studies at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, alongside several other teachers. From 2010 to 2013, he was attested as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt.

Stephen Prothero, a religious studies scholar, studied at Yale University and Harvard University, completing his PhD under William R. Hutchison in 1990. Around 1996, he was appointed C. Allyn and Elizabeth V. Russell Professor Emeritus of Religion in America at Boston University.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1978–1986). A scholar of Sinology and religious studies, he taught at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) and became Professor of Chinese at Arizona State University around 2007.
Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Stephen Wootton Bushell studied medicine at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London (MD 1868). Active in Sinology and archaeology, his early career included posts at Guy's Hospital (1866) and Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

Steve Odin studied at Stony Brook University (~1975–1980) under Robert Cummings Neville and others. A specialist in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, he became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1982.

Steven Collins earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Bristol (~1979–1987), Indiana University (~1987–1991), and became Chester D. Tripp Professor in the Humanities at Chicago in 1991.
Steven Edward Lindquist, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2005 under Patrick Olivelle. He later held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, he taught at Villanova, La Salle, and Penn State before becoming Professor at Florida International University in 1997.

Steven Lukes studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. A scholar of philosophy, he held posts at Balliol College (1966–1987), European University Institute (1995–1996), LSE (~1999–2001), and served as Professor at New York University (~2002–2021).

Steven Weinberger studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins in 2003. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 2006).
Stewart McFarlane is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held posts at Lancaster University, attested in 1991 and in 2001 within the Department of Religious Studies.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, he held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University, and Stony Brook University (~2018).

Stig Wikander studied at Uppsala under H. S. Nyberg, later serving as docent at Lund (1941–1953) and Chair of Sanskrit and Comparative Indo-European Philology at Uppsala (1953–1974). His fields were Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies.
Stuart H. Blackburn studied at Wesleyan University and the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1980). A scholar of Indology, he held a post at SOAS University of London around 1994.

Stuart Piggott studied at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1935–1936). A scholar in archaeology and Indology, he held a post at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1946 to 1977.
Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.
